summary.prose: This Story adds a model family to insrc's shipped model definitions: the Claude tool on Ollama. It declares that its tool runs on Ollama, and every model it lists is marked cloud or local. The daemon validates it, serves it in the definitions answer every client reads, and resolves a tier on it only to a declared model; an undeclared model is refused with the reason 'model-not-supported' instead of being replaced. Today's three families, and every place that today means 'a vendor CLI family', keep their behaviour.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Model the new runner as a new family in the model definitions (alternative a1). The definitions file, its validator and the definitions answer gain one family, 'ollama-claude', with the CLI kind 'claude' and a host mark 'ollama'; every model of that family carries a hosting mark, 'cloud' or 'local'. Tier settings, effort filtering and provider construction keep their one per-family path. A family with the Ollama host mark builds the existing CLI provider with an Ollama target applied to that subprocess only, and clients use the host mark to show cloud/local and to never offer unlisted model ids for that family. Scope change 2026-10-29 (user decision): the Codex-on-Ollama family is withdrawn, because Ollama's cloud models ignore a requested output format and the Codex tool depends on it (DEF non-goal, citation c9 of the DEF).

ownedContracts.name: Ollama-hosted CLI families in the definitions answer
ownedContracts.purpose: The wire shape every consumer reads to know the new family, that it runs a CLI on Ollama, and which of its models are cloud or local.

ownedContracts.name: Tier resolution on an Ollama-hosted family
ownedContracts.purpose: How the daemon reports the tier it actually runs when the tier names a host family, including a model the definitions do not declare, so the run layer and every settings surface show the same outcome.

boundary.internal: The shipped definitions entry for the new family and its models (which cloud and local models are supported), the catalog validator's four-member check and the 'hosting required on host families' rule, the registry's mapping from a CLI client to its direct family only, and the refusal of the unknown-model check and the approved-model store for host families stay inside s1.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: How the CLI provider points a run at Ollama (the claude environment, applied only to that subprocess), the pre-run checks that Ollama answers and the model is available or signed in for a cloud model, the failure messages that name the cause, and the time limit that keeps a run from waiting forever stay inside s2.
The terminal UI's runner list, model list with cloud/local labels, effort step and the withheld 'enter another id' path for host families, and its display of the resolved tier, stay inside s3.

The VS Code tier picker's family and model steps, the settings write validation that refuses an undeclared model for a host family, the cloud/local labels and the withheld 'enter another id' item stay inside s4.
The JetBrains Settings page's family and model selectors, the cloud/local labels, the filter that keeps host families out of the model-check flow, and its display of the resolved tier stay inside s5.

nonFunctional.performance: No added cost on today's runners. A run on a host family adds one Ollama reachability and model-availability check before the CLI starts; a run never waits beyond the existing CLI time limit.
nonFunctional.security: The Ollama settings are applied only to the started subprocess's environment or arguments; the user's own CLI configuration files and the daemon's environment are never changed. No API key is stored; the claude CLI gets the placeholder token Ollama accepts locally.
nonFunctional.observability: The daemon logs the family, model, hosting and Ollama target of each host-family run, and a failed pre-run check logs which check failed; the tier resolution reported to clients names a 'model-not-supported' fallback.
nonFunctional.durability: Nothing new is persisted: tier settings keep their stored shape, and the new families live in the shipped definitions file.

dataModelChanges.details: The closed family-id union and FAMILY_IDS grow from three to four members: 'ollama-claude' joins 'cli-claude', 'cli-codex' and 'ollama'. CliFamilyId keeps meaning the two vendor CLI families; a new HostFamilyId names the host family.
Adds host?: 'ollama'. Present only on the host family, which also carries cliKind and carries neither tierDefaults nor summariserModel.
Adds hosting?: 'cloud' | 'local'. Required on every model of a host family, absent on every other model.

model becomes optional and FallbackReason gains 'model-not-supported'. model is undefined only for a host family whose configured model is not declared; the existing fallback field name 'requested' is kept (the sc2 sketch's 'configured' names the same value).
The answer carries host on a host family and hosting on each of its models, exactly as sc1 sketches.

Appends one family after the existing three: ollama-claude (cliKind 'claude', host 'ollama'). It lists only models that returned a schema-checked answer through the Claude tool on Ollama in a probe, each with hosting and its efforts. The first batch (user decision 2026-10-29), all probed on 2026-10-29 and all hosting 'cloud': deepseek-v4-pro:cloud, deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud, glm-5.3:cloud, glm-5.3-flash:cloud, mistral-large-4:cloud and kimi-k3:cloud. Each model's efforts follow the thinking levels Ollama reports for it: glm-5.3, glm-5.3-flash, deepseek-v4.1-flash and kimi-k3 list low, high and max; deepseek-v4-pro and mistral-large-4 only switch thinking on or off, so they list none.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: The catalog types, validator, registry and projectDefinitions add host and hosting exactly as sketched; the five-member FamilyId is the sketch's union. Sites that mean 'a vendor CLI family' switch from 'id is not ollama' or 'has a CLI kind' to 'has a CLI kind and no host', per the HLD's classification rule: isCliFamily (src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:140), the unknown-model check gate (src/daemon/model-check.ts:319), the unlisted/rejected fallback (src/daemon/model-registry.ts:277-278), the tier write's model check (src/daemon/config-write.ts:74), familyForClient (src/daemon/model-registry.ts:105), attribution by label prefix (src/workflow/attribution.ts:49) and the projection's rejectedModels decision (src/daemon/model-definitions.ts:104, used at :117-119), so rejectedModels appears only on vendor CLI families while installed stays on the family without a CLI kind. The approved-model store already refuses other families (src/daemon/model-registry.ts:142). Sites that mean 'runs a CLI' (the provider-factory and listing sites) stay on cliKind.

resolveTier returns model undefined with fallback reason 'model-not-supported' for a host family's undeclared model and never substitutes. resolveTierWith logs it; tierModelOf reports the requested id with the fallback so clients show what was set and why it is not used; the build-step validate fallback, which only resolves the default vendor family, keeps a required model. The fallback keeps today's field name 'requested'.

errorCases.scenario: A host family entry in the definitions file lacks host or cliKind, carries tierDefaults or summariserModel, or has a model without hosting.
errorCases.detection: validateFamily checks a host family's shape when the file is loaded (the replacement of isCliFamily at src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:140-142 and the checks at :186-191).
errorCases.response: Throws ModelCatalogValidationError naming the family and the faulty field, as for today's families.
errorCases.userImpact: The daemon refuses to start with a message naming the bad entry; this only happens with a broken shipped file, which the asset test catches before release.

errorCases.scenario: hosting appears on a model of a family that has no host.
errorCases.detection: validateFamily rejects hosting on any model of a family without host.
errorCases.userImpact: Same as above: caught by the asset test before release.

errorCases.scenario: A tier names a host family with a model the definitions do not declare for it (for example a hand-edited config, or a model removed in a later release).
errorCases.detection: resolveTier finds no model of that id or alias in the host family (registry find at src/daemon/model-registry.ts:269).
errorCases.response: Returns model undefined and fallback { reason: 'model-not-supported', requested }; resolveTierWith logs a warning naming the tier, family and requested model. No other model or family is substituted.
errorCases.userImpact: The tier is shown as not supported in the settings surfaces and the run layer (s2) refuses to run it with that reason, rather than running a model the user did not choose.

errorCases.scenario: A caller asks for the unknown-model check or an approved-model profile on a host family.

errorCases.userImpact: Host families stay limited to their declared models (k1).

migrationSteps.action: Add the optional host field to family definitions and hosting to model definitions, the new id to the family-id set, and the 'model-not-supported' reason; make TierResolution.model optional and make its three readers handle absence.
Replace the 'id is not ollama' and 'has a CLI kind' tests at the vendor-family sites with 'has a CLI kind and no host'; keep the 'runs a CLI' sites on the CLI kind.
Add the host-family validation rules and grow the validator test fixture to four families.
Append the host family with its declared models to the shipped definitions file, after the existing three.
Project host and hosting in the definitions answer.

migration.backwardCompat: Additive for clients: the answer gains optional host and hosting fields and one family; existing entries are byte-identical. Stored tier settings keep their shape and existing tiers resolve as before. Clients that do not yet read host would list the new family and could offer 'Enter another model id' for them, but the daemon refuses an unlisted model for a host family (model-not-supported) and the unknown-model check refuses host families, so no undeclared model runs; s3-s5 remove that offer.

alternativesConsidered.name: Optional model only on a host-family refusal (sc2 as sketched)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: One host family in the closed family set; TierResolution.model becomes optional and is absent only when the host family names an undeclared model, with fallback reason 'model-not-supported'.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
The catalog's family-id set grows by 'ollama-claude'. CliFamilyId keeps meaning the two vendor CLI families; a new HostFamilyId names the host family. FamilyDefinition gains host?: 'ollama' and ModelDefinition gains hosting?: 'cloud' | 'local'. Validation replaces the 'id !== ollama' test with the family's shape: a host family needs cliKind, host and hosting on every model, and must not carry tierDefaults or summariserModel; a vendor CLI family keeps today's rules. The shipped file appends the host family after the existing three, so readers that take the first family with a CLI kind keep picking the vendor family.

The registry exposes host(family) and returns hosting on resolved models. resolveTier keeps today's path for the three existing families; for a host family, a declared model resolves as usual and an undeclared one returns { family, model: undefined, fallback: { reason: 'model-not-supported', requested } } with no substitute. familyForClient, the approved-model store and the unknown-model check consider vendor families only. projectDefinitions adds host on the family and hosting on each model of a host family. resolveTierWith logs the refusal, and tierModelOf reports the configured id so clients show what was set and why it is not used.
pros: Matches the approved sc2 sketch: a refused model has no model and an explicit reason, so nothing silently runs a different model.
The three existing families keep their resolution and fallback unchanged; the optional model is reachable only through a host family.
Clients get both the configured id and the reason, which is what s3-s5 must show.
cons: TierResolution.model becomes optional, so every reader of resolution.model must handle absence: resolveTierWith, tierModelOf and the build-step validate fallback.
The run layer (s2) must refuse to build a provider for a resolution without a model.

alternativesConsidered.name: Required model with an in-family substitute
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep TierResolution.model required: an undeclared model on a host family falls back to that family's first declared model, flagged 'model-not-supported'.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
Same family set, marks and validator rule as a1. resolveTier, on an undeclared host-family model, substitutes the first model the family declares and reports fallback 'model-not-supported'. No consumer changes type.

The definitions answer and the client-to-family mapping are as in a1.
pros: No optional field: every existing consumer of TierResolution keeps compiling unchanged.
A tier on a host family always has a model to run.
cons: Runs a model the user did not choose, possibly cloud instead of local or the reverse, which conflicts with ac3 ('the model is not used') only in spirit but with k1's intent that only chosen declared models run.
Departs from the approved sc2 sketch (model undefined), so it needs an HLD amendment.
File order becomes a behaviour: reordering the shipped models changes which model runs.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Scores 'partial' on ac3 (it silently runs an unchosen model from file order) and 'violates' sc2 (model stays required with a substitute).

alternativesConsidered.name: Separate unsupported-resolution type
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: resolveTier returns either today's TierResolution or a distinct UnsupportedTierResolution for a host family's undeclared model.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
Same family set, marks and validator rule as a1. resolveTier's return type becomes a union of TierResolution (model required) and UnsupportedTierResolution { family, requested, reason: 'model-not-supported' } discriminated by a kind field.

Every caller narrows the union; the definitions answer is as in a1.
pros: The type system forces every caller to handle the refused case explicitly.
cons: A new union return type plus a discriminant touches every caller's control flow, more change than a1 for the same behaviour.
Departs from the sc2 sketch's single TierResolution shape.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Scores 'partial' on sc2: a union return shape instead of the single TierResolution, with more caller churn for the same behaviour as a1.
